spec: Build a blog platform backend. Authors create posts with markdown bodies stored in DynamoDB and images stored in S3. Readers can list and read posts and submit comments. Comments are not published immediately: they are placed on an SQS moderation queue, and an approval endpoint pops them from moderation into the published comments table.

complexity.rationale: Content, media, and queued moderation form a multi-stage publication workflow.

congruence_checklist: DynamoDB storage for posts and comments
SQS moderation queue for new comments
GET endpoints listing and reading posts

plan.summary: A FastAPI backend for a small blog platform. Authors create, update and delete markdown posts persisted in DynamoDB and upload post images to an S3 bucket. Readers list and read published posts and submit comments; submitted comments are not written to the published comments table directly but are enqueued as JSON messages on an SQS moderation queue. Moderators poll a moderation endpoint that receives messages from the queue and use an approval endpoint to either persist the comment into the published comments DynamoDB table (approve) or discard it (reject); in both cases the SQS message is deleted using its receipt handle. The service runs as a standalone process and calls DynamoDB, S3 and SQS directly with boto3.

endpoints.purpose: Liveness/readiness probe reporting that the service and its AWS clients are reachable.
Create a new post with title, markdown body, author and tags; writes an item to the posts DynamoDB table and returns the generated post_id.
List posts with pagination (limit plus next_token) and optional status filter; scans/queries the posts DynamoDB table.
Read a single post including its markdown body and image URLs from the posts DynamoDB table.
Update an existing post's title, markdown body, tags or publication status in DynamoDB.
Delete a post item from DynamoDB (associated images remain in S3 unless deleted separately).
Upload an image file (multipart/form-data) to the S3 images bucket under the post's prefix and record the object key on the post item.
List the S3 object keys for a post's images and return time-limited presigned GET URLs for each.
Reader submits a comment; the payload is validated and sent as a JSON message to the SQS moderation queue and returns status 'pending_moderation' with a comment_id.
List published (approved) comments for a post by querying the comments DynamoDB table partitioned by post_id.
Moderator polls pending comments by receiving a batch of messages from the SQS moderation queue; returns comment payloads together with their receipt handles.
Approve a pending comment: writes it into the published comments DynamoDB table and deletes the message from SQS using the supplied receipt handle.
Reject a pending comment: deletes the message from the SQS moderation queue without persisting it, optionally recording a rejection reason in the log.

data_models.name: PendingComment
fields: receipt_handle (string, returned by the moderation poll endpoint only)

aws_resources.name: blog-posts
aws_resources.justification: Stores post items (markdown body, metadata, image key list) written and read by the /posts endpoints; partition key post_id.

aws_resources.name: blog-published-comments
aws_resources.justification: Stores comments only after moderation approval; queried by the GET /posts/{post_id}/comments endpoint using partition key post_id and sort key comment_id.

aws_resources.name: blog-post-images
aws_resources.justification: Holds uploaded post images written by POST /posts/{post_id}/images and served through presigned GET URLs.

aws_resources.name: blog-comment-moderation-queue
aws_resources.justification: Holds submitted comments awaiting moderation; written by the comment submission endpoint and consumed/deleted by the moderation poll and approve/reject endpoints.

aws_resources.name: blog-comment-moderation-dlq
aws_resources.justification: Redrive target for the moderation queue so comments that repeatedly fail moderation processing are retained rather than lost.

aws_resources.name: blog-backend-app-policy
aws_resources.justification: Least-privilege policy/role granting the standalone backend service DynamoDB read/write on the two tables, S3 object read/write on the images bucket, and SQS send/receive/delete on the moderation queue.

aws_resources.name: blog-backend-logs
aws_resources.justification: Log group where the backend emits application and moderation-audit logs for post creation, image upload and comment approval/rejection events.

assumptions: No Lambda or API Gateway is planned: the moderation workflow is driven synchronously by operator-called HTTP endpoints on the standalone backend, so there is no cloud-side event processing to host.

Authentication/authorisation is out of scope; the author identity is taken from an optional X-Author header or the request body, and moderation endpoints are assumed to be reachable only by trusted operators.
Markdown bodies are stored inline as a DynamoDB string attribute (assumed under the 400 KB item limit) rather than offloaded to S3.
Post listing uses a DynamoDB scan with a LastEvaluatedKey-based next_token because the spec implies a small, single-tenant blog with no secondary access patterns.
Images are uploaded through the API as multipart/form-data and the backend puts them into S3; reads are served via presigned URLs (default 1 hour TTL) because the bucket stays private.

'Popping' a comment from moderation is implemented as SQS ReceiveMessage plus DeleteMessage with the receipt handle supplied by the moderator; the queue visibility timeout is assumed to be 30 seconds and the client must approve/reject within that window or re-poll.
Comment IDs are server-generated UUIDs assigned at submission time so the same identifier survives from moderation into the published comments table.
Deleting a post does not cascade-delete its images or published comments; the spec does not require cleanup semantics.
Region and endpoint configuration (LocalStack) are supplied to the backend via environment variables such as AWS_REGION and AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, along with the table, bucket and queue names.
No Secrets Manager or SNS resources are planned because the spec involves no credentials or notification fan-out.

events: 🧭 Parsed specification → blog_platform_backend (fastapi); AWS resources: DynamoDB:blog-posts, DynamoDB:blog-published-comments, S3:blog-post-images, SQS:blog-comment-moderation-queue, SQS:blog-comment-moderation-dlq, IAM:blog-backend-app-policy, CloudWatch:blog-backend-logs

🐍 Generated application code (initial): 7 files — FastAPI blog backend split into app.py (routes/models), storage.py (boto3 DynamoDB/S3/SQS behind injectable classes with StorageError translation, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL + us-east-1 defaults, env-driven resource names) and uploads.py (stdlib multipart/raw body parsing so no python-multipart dependency is needed). All 13 planned endpoints are implemented, including the SQS-backed comment moderation poll/approve/reject flow. tests/test_app.py exercises every endpoint via TestClient with in-memory fakes injected through dependency_overrides, plus unit tests of the storage layer with fully stubbed boto3 clients — no network or LocalStack required.

🏗️ Generated Terraform (initial): 4 files — Terraform for the blog platform backend, tracing one-for-one to the plan's aws_resources: two DynamoDB tables (blog-posts with post_id hash key; blog-published-comments with post_id/comment_id) each with point-in-time recovery and server-side encryption; a private blog-post-images S3 bucket with versioning, SSE, full public-access block, ownership controls, lifecycle rules and server access logging into a dedicated (equally hardened) log bucket with a scoped delivery policy; an SQS moderation queue with SSE-SQS, a 30s visibility timeout matching the plan and a redrive policy to a matching SSE-enabled DLQ (plus redrive_allow_policy); a CloudWatch log group with 365-day retention; and a least-privilege IAM role/policy granting only the specific DynamoDB item/query/scan actions on the two table ARNs, ListBucket/GetBucketLocation on the bucket plus Get/Put/DeleteObject on its objects, send/receive/delete/visibility on the queue ARNs, and log-stream writes on the log group ARN — no wildcard actions or resources. No Lambda, API Gateway, SNS, Secrets Manager or unsupported services are created, matching the plan's assumptions; provider pins hashicorp/aws ~> 5.0 with default_tags for project and managed-by, and KMS-CMK-specific Checkov checks are explicitly skipped with reasons because LocalStack Community deployment uses AWS-managed/SSE-S3/SSE-SQS encryption.
